values: 208 model/major-version entries covering Fender tube guitar amps, 1946–2026. Broad catalog, not a verified exhaustive SKU register.
Tube preamp and tube power amplifier. Solid-state rectifiers, switching and ancillary effects do not exclude an amp. Digital-preamp or solid-state-power hybrids are excluded.

Vintage Bassmans widely used for guitar; guitar/steel Vibrasonic and Vibrosonic models. Princeton Recording, Champ 12 and Vibro Champ Reverb have non-tube ancillary processing, identified in their notes.

Dedicated bass-only amplifiers, acoustic amps, PA systems, separate reverb units, speaker-only cabinets, pedals, K&F predecessors, prototypes and non-Fender brands. Super Champ XD/X2, Vibro Champ XD, Champ 25, VM, Cyber and digital Tone Master models are excluded.

Major circuit/era changes are separate rows. Many cosmetic editions, speakers, finishes, regional versions, head/combo configurations and limited packages are grouped. Not every circuit subrevision or dealer-exclusive SKU is a separate entry.

Introduced/production-through years are approximate historical catalog windows. Transition years overlap; shipment dates and regional availability differ. Current denotes a continuing product family, not verified stock everywhere. Approximate or uncertain endings are marked.

Introduction year ascending, then maximum/representative output watts ascending, then name. This prioritizes age over size. Use the wattage filter/sort to see all small amps first across every era. Physical dimensions are not the size measure.
Cabinet means combo/head format and stock speaker count × nominal diameter in inches. Head prices exclude the external cabinet. No dimensions or wood species are implied unless stated.
Representative audio output in watts, not wall-power consumption or speaker power handling. Ratings, distortion thresholds and circuit revisions vary. Variable-power models use their maximum rating.

Nominal factory internal-speaker load for combos, or selected output load for heads. These are reference values, not a blanket list of allowed extension-cabinet combinations. Consult the exact model manual and rear-panel marking before connecting a cabinet. Vintage speakers/output transformers may have been replaced.
Historical 3.2Ω speaker ratings are often rounded to the modern 4Ω class. Champ-related rows note this distinction. Three-speaker and six-speaker arrangements can have non-integer total loads.
November 19, 2026. A source URL does not mean every specification in that row was independently verified. Historical and grouped rows require exact-revision confirmation.

USD for working used examples in ordinary good-to-excellent condition, unless explicitly labeled new. Excludes tax, shipping and cabinet for a head. Condition, original transformers/speakers, modifications and provenance can move prices substantially.

Published used-value/sold ranges are explicitly labeled and linked. Most other rows are indicative estimates, not verified current transaction ranges. Those estimates should be refreshed with exact-model sold comparables before budgeting. Blank means a reliable current price was not established.
Woodies, early Twins, rare signatures and decorative Custom Shop packages have sparse comparables. Their broad estimates are especially provisional; obtain an individual appraisal.

Qualitative editorial estimate of availability, not audited production totals and not a value ranking. Common: regularly encountered. Uncommon: available with searching. Rare: infrequent. Very rare: scarce short-run or early surviving examples.
For a model of interest, confirm the circuit/version first, then its load and stock speakers, and refresh pricing from recent sold listings. Use the source archive to select the exact owner manual.

Row-by-row review added. Review status: Corrected = a value was changed (see Changes). Confirmed = production years, and specs or prices where noted, matched an outside source. Reviewed, not source-checked = read for plausibility only. Added = new row researched on November 20, 2026. The 1946 Pro reissue row was removed and nine rows were added, so the count is 208.

Production through is split into Production end year and Production status. Load type says whether the load is fixed, selectable or varies by configuration. Price confidence: High = published sold or used-value range; Medium = observed asking prices; Low = indicative estimate; None = no used range. Era group collapses the 24 era labels into 11.
Fender list price for models in the current catalog, first-listed finish, read November 20, 2026 from the Fender Vintage & Pro Tube collection. Used prices remain in the Low and High columns.
